description.value:
"You are not an animal that learned to talk. You are a story the world made into a person because it needed you in the room."

Folklore Presence. 1/Soma Break, when you first meet a community, decide whether the rumors about you arrived first. If yes, reroll the lowest die on your first Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) check with anyone in that community (your choice which skill, declared when you roll). The rumor is not always flattering — the GM gets to colour it.

Wasteland Adapted. Reroll the lowest die on defense checks against disease and environmental poison. You can subsist on rations that would sicken most humans (spoiled meat, swamp water, mushroom flesh).

Survivor's Instinct. 1/Soma Break, when you would drop to 0 Integrity, you may instead drop to 1 Integrity and gain one level of Stress.

Cryptidkin Subspecies. This heritage preserves the original UUID for Jackalope (Bad Eden) while converting it from a species-root to a Cryptidkin subspecies.

“You don’t spot a Jackalope. You notice the world flinch, and then realize why.”

Jackalope. Fast because they have to be. Twitchy because the world has trained them that stillness is how you die. Half-remembered pre-Shattering folklore, half radiation-assembled rumor, and fully people.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium.

  • Speed. 7 squares

  • Subspecies Lean. Your subspecies leans toward INTR (Intrigue)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Folklore & Frame

At creation you gain Folklore & Frame (Folklore Presence, Wasteland Adapted, Survivor’s Instinct).

Jackalope Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17). Jackalope powers emphasize: Startle Reflex (can’t-be-caught-flat burst), Wasteland Bound (long-distance run), Horns of Bad Luck (jinx aura), Can’t Catch Me (evasion), and strategic Bad Omen Runner faction hooks.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

If you see Jackalope tracks circling your hex, you are not under attack. You are being advised.

  • OP Edge. Your faction gains +1 Soft Power OP and +1 Non-Lethal OP at campaign start.

  • Trail Whisper. Once per Strategic Turn, your faction can reroll a single Travel or Scout check made in a hex adjacent to your home territory.

description.value:
"You aren't fast because you're fast. You're fast because the world keeps deciding to miss."

Startle Reflex (1/Soma Break). Reaction when you are targeted by an attack roll or fail an Intrigue check — move up to 2 squares without provoking opportunity attacks.

Horns of Bad Luck. Your natural horns ship as a Jackalope-only Manifestation when you take the heritage — see your Manifestations tab. When violence escalates around you, the GM may describe unsettling omens tied to your presence — a mirror crack, a dropped knife, a candle going out the wrong direction.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — Startle Reflex Recovery: 1/Soma Break  ·  Action: Reaction  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke. When targeted by an attack roll or you fail an Intrigue check, move up to 2 squares without provoking opportunity attacks.

"You're already moving. The fight rearranges around it."

The Shadow Courier runs on Surge, like everyone — but yours comes from motion. Move 30+ ft in a turn and you bank +1 Surge (again at 12 squares, max +2/round). A courier in motion has options; a courier standing still is just a target. The old Pace pool folds into this — same fuel, one number.

The Courier (spent via Surge)

  • Courier's Step (1) — +half-speed move (no provoke) and a freed reaction; flow through the fight.
  • Ghoststep (3) — DR equal to Tier till your next turn, and reposition out of danger.
  • Flank & Strike (5) — reposition, then your next Strike reroll the lowest die and +Tier d6.
  • No Such Door (8) — allies within Tier squares each gain a freed reaction and a reroll; open the road for the whole team.

The Package endures as your work — designate it, carry it, deliver it. Delivery banks your Surge to full and still triggers the route's strategic payoff (Intrigue OP, Darkness reduction, the arrival that mattered).

description.value:
You cross what isn't supposed to be crossed — and you always come out the other side carrying something.

On gaining Shadow Courier Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Stealth (Intrigue).

  • Skill rank +1 in Tinkering (Intrigue).

  • Intrigue OP cap +2 and Logistics OP cap +2 on the faction your character belongs to.

  • Pace pool comes online (movement-generated). Max = max(2, ceil((Intrigue value + Shadow Courier Initiation) / 3)), capped at 8. Refills on Soma Break and on Package delivery.

  • Package slot comes online — one Package at a time, type set by your chosen Route at L1.

Pace generation. Gain 1 Pace when you move at least 6 squares on your turn. Maximum 1 Pace generated per turn from this feature. Doctrine features may add their own generators.

Baseline Pace spends (free action, 1 Pace each):

  • Move 5 extra feet without spending an action.

  • Reroll a single Stealth (Intrigue), Athletics (Violence), or Tinkering (Intrigue) check — keep the new result.

  • Ignore a single reaction strike against you on this turn.

Liminal Sense. Once per encounter, ignore the first detection-style roll an opponent attempts against you (perception, scrying, Insight to read your intent, etc.). The roll is treated as if it had failed; resources spent on the attempt are not refunded.

Cryptidkin. Normalized Bad Eden ancestry root.

Select one subspecies when building the character: Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin.

This root grants the shared Cryptidkin core trait package. Subspecies layer flavor, size, and Tier powers on top.

“Every settlement has a story about you. None of them are accurate. All of them are useful.”

Cryptidkin Core Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Cryptidkin).

  • Size. Small or Medium (set by subspecies).

  • Speed. 6 squares (subspecies may override).

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Cryptidkin does not grant fixed bonuses. Subspecies lean expressed through Tier powers.

Folklore Presence. When you first encounter an NPC group, the GM chooses (or rolls) whether you are met as omen, trophy, or legend. It is never neutral. People have heard of your kind. They are almost always wrong, and that is almost always useful.

Wasteland Adapted. You reroll the lowest die on checks against disease and environmental poison. You ignore the first nonmagical environmental hazard you encounter each Strategic Turn (heat, cold, radiation taint, wind shear, fume pockets).

Survivor’s Instinct. When you roll initiative, you can choose to know the position of the nearest exit, the nearest threat, or the nearest ally within 12 squares You cannot be surprised while conscious.

Subspecies. Choose one Cryptidkin subspecies (Chupacabra, Jackalope, Furrykin). Your subspecies grants Tier powers as you level (Tier I at creation, then 5/11/17).

Crew Type (Bad Eden): Covert Ops Cell.

“If you saw it happen, it wasn’t us.”

Covert Ops cells make wars quiet. They prefer locks to speeches, shadows to banners, and results to credit. They don’t start fights—they rearrange the board so the fight never happens.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Stealth and with the Tinkering aptitude.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Intrigue OPs.

“You do not wave your hands and hope. You know what symbols are for.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): The Magician (Scholar). Researcher, operator, and wielder of applied understanding. You turn knowledge into leverage and leverage into effect.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. This Archetype is associated with +1 Intrigue in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for the full tactical and strategic expression of scholarship, arcane literacy, research throughput, and recovered knowledge.

description.value:
Occult Association (Bad Eden): Tarot Mage.

“The future is rude. I read it anyway.”

Tarot Mages do not predict the future. They interrogate it.

They treat fate like a deck: shuffled by chaos, cut by will, and stacked by anyone reckless enough to pay the price. Where other occult traditions pursue the Great Work through doctrine, continuity, or purification, the Tarot Mage pursues it through timing. The right pressure, at the right instant, can do what a thousand sincere speeches cannot.

To a Tarot Mage, the Great Work is not just about choosing well. It is about choosing at the moment that matters.

How Tarot Mages pursue the Great Work:

  • By reading currents before Scenarios begin
  • By turning uncertainty into leverage
  • By making coincidence behave like a trained animal
  • By treating timing as a resource as real as OP

Resonance: Keter / Signal / Probability — possibility, timing, pattern emergence, and the dangerous urge to edit what has not happened yet.

Tell-tales: shuffles anything that can be shuffled — cards, choices, people.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 to Intrigue OP rolls

Cost Principle: fate does not like fingerprints. Expect backlash, strange timing, narrative inversion, and consequences that arrive sideways when you push probability too hard.

Mercy - Expansion without fear. +1 Diplomacy, +1 Culture OPs

Chesed creates room for others to live, recover, and belong. It rewards community-building, morale recovery, and factions that grow stronger by sheltering rather than merely surviving.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Magician

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Occult and Lore. You learn one Tier-0 manifestation from the Wizard manifestation list.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

You’re learning the shape of your shadow. Expect mistakes. Budget for them.

Tier 1 — Tarot Mage

“The future is rude. I read it anyway.”

You are not powerful yet. You are noticeable. The cards do not obey you, but they do answer — and that is already enough to make normal people uncomfortable.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • 1/Soma Break, before making an attribute check, you may draw the line of fate early and gain Advantage on that check

Strategic (Faction Scale)

Cost: once you start consulting fate, you begin seeing patterns everywhere. Expect second-guessing, omen pressure, or trouble distinguishing signal from appetite.

Before an attribute check, reroll the lowest die on it.

Bladed Tempo

Your weapons are punctuation.

Rules

When you hit with a melee weapon attack, you may immediately draw or stow a weapon, or shift 1 square without provoking reaction strikes.

Disciplined Fire

It’s not about more shots. It’s about the right shot.

Rules

Once per turn when you hit with a ranged weapon attack, you may choose one:

  • Pin: The target’s movement is reduced by 2 squares until the start of your next turn.
  • Disrupt: The next attack roll the target makes before the end of its next turn is made with keep-lowest.

A creature can be affected by this principle only once per round.

description.value:
Signature move. Once a scene, the membrane chooses you instead of the wall.

The Crossing — 1/scene (recovers on Soma Break). As an action, declare a single threshold within reach: a door, wall, ward, alarm, divination perimeter, hex boundary, or similar barrier. You cross it. Resolution depends on the barrier:

  • Mundane barriers (locked doors, sealed walls, alarmed corridors, password gates) simply fail to register your passage. No roll. The barrier remains intact for everyone else.

  • Magical wards or alarms (alarm manifestations, divination perimeters, scrying screens, hex-warded boundaries) require an Intrigue defense check against DC 12 + (the ward source's Initiation tier × 2). On a success you cross without triggering the ward; on a failure you still cross, but the ward fires normally and the source is alerted.

Several Route doctrines extend or modify The Crossing — see your doctrine's L5 feature.

Focused Execution

You take your time. Just long enough to matter.

Rules

Before making a ranged weapon attack, declare a Focused Shot: you ignore half cover, and if the attack hits you add your skill rank bonus to the damage roll. If the attack misses, your movement is reduced by 2 squares until the end of your next turn.

Delivery is a sacrament now.

At Shadow Courier Initiation 11, your Route's signature Package type gains an additional benefit each time you successfully deliver it (in addition to the L1 doctrine delivery effect):

  • Route of the Wayfarer Tongue (Message). Delivering grants the recipient faction +1 Intrigue OP in addition to the L1 effect.

  • Route of the Last Mile (Soul). Delivering reduces Darkness in the recipient's hex by an additional 1 point in addition to the L1 effect.

If you ever change Routes (which the campaign should not normally permit), this feature retunes itself to the new doctrine on your next Soma Break.

description.value:
Every threshold you have ever crossed remembers you. You may now ask one to remember you out loud.

Unfound Route — 1/session. As an action, name two thresholds you have personally crossed earlier in this campaign (any door, arch, gate, ward, or hex boundary your character has crossed at least once before). You travel from one to the other directly, by way of the spaces in between that don't exist on any map.

  • You may bring up to 4 willing allies with you.

  • The journey takes one hour of subjective time regardless of actual distance, terrain, hostility, or planar boundary. You arrive somewhat changed by the experience.

  • The destination threshold must still exist (not destroyed, sealed against you specifically, or relocated).

  • You cannot use Unfound Route to enter a place you have not been, to escape an active combat round, or to cross a threshold someone else used (only your own).

Pressure Tested

Surviving the hit gives you leverage.

Rules

When you succeed on a defense check against an effect that would impose a condition, you may choose to ignore the effect entirely or reroll the lowest die on your next attack or checks before the end of your next turn. Once per Respite.

Threat Assessment

You don’t look at enemies. You read them.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Perception (Mind) or Investigation (Mind) (your choice). If you are already proficient, you gain mastery instead. Additionally, at the start of combat you may ask the GM: which enemy appears most dangerous, most injured, or is controlling the battlefield?

"You came through a door that wasn't for them."

Doctrine: Thresholds weaponized — covert, predatory; who gets through and who really, really doesn't.

The Black Stair is the courier as ambush. Your Surge spends turn crossings into kills: strike from where they weren't watching, slam the threshold shut on a foe, and spring the stair that does not end.

Route (spent via Surge)

  • Ambush (1) — your next Strike +Tier d6; the target's next attack is at disadvantage.

  • Cut Off (2) — a foe is Staggered and cannot take reactions until your next turn.

  • Stair-Trap (5) — your next Strike lands as a max-die crit and knocks the target Prone; if it drops them, you regain a freed action.
